maya (FinOps): Heads-up — I noticed a large variance in the Asia GPU spend this month: reserved vs spot split changed ~42% vs last month. Can we get a team-by-team + SKU breakdown? Need to update forecasts and reserved commitments.

ashish (Infra): Which billing export did you look at? invoice lines or the raw usage export? Can you paste the row or a link? :mag_right:

maya (FinOps): Pasted the BigQuery export row here — looks like multiple sku lines under asia-south1. Example query I used:
```sql
SELECT sku_description, project_id, SUM(cost) as cost, SUM(usage_hours) as hours
FROM `billing.gcp_line_items`
WHERE invoice_month = '2026-03' AND region LIKE 'asia-%'
GROUP BY sku_description, project_id
ORDER BY cost DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

priya (CostOps): Running that now. Preliminary result: large preemptible / spot hours spike starting 2026-03-02 — likely CI batch jobs hitting spot pools. I'll export CSV and drop in GCS.

jordan (Platform): We did a test increase to batch-processing throughput on 3/1 and auto-scale to spot pools — that would increase hours but lower $/hour. We should show net cost (cost/hour * hours) vs reserved baseline. I can share the infra job IDs. @ashish can confirm which projects used the spot pools.

ashish (Infra): Confirmed: projects infra-batch-asia & experiments-ml consumed the bulk on spot instances. autoscaler policy scaled min=0 -> max=40 GPUs for 24h window on several days. tickets: INF-4389.

ken (SRE): On-call saw increased preemptions around 03/03 and 03/07 which caused retries and some job restarts — that may explain extra wall hours. Eviction rate went from ~3% -> ~12% those days.

finance-bot: Billing report generated: gs://redwood-billing/exports/2026-03/asia-sku-breakdown.csv (sha256: a3f4...)

priya (CostOps): Dropped a short CSV summary in GCS with columns: project_id, team, sku, hours, cost. Quick peek: infra-batch-asia (team: Platform) = 7,800 GPU-hours, $58k; experiments-ml (team: Research) = 4,200 GPU-hours, $31k; reserved discounts currently applied only to infra-batch-asia for some SKUs.

maya (FinOps): Thanks. Two asks: 1) Can Platform and Research confirm which workloads are persistent (candidates for reservation) vs ephemeral? 2) We need a recommendation on whether to purchase partial reserved capacity for asia-south1 or rely on spot savings but with risk of retries.

jordan (Platform): Platform: infra-batch-asia has a mix — ~60% persistent nightly batches (candidate for reservation), 40% experimental/ephemeral. I'll open an infra ticket to split those into separate projects and tag them with team=billing_owner.

ashish (Infra): Short-term mitigation: tighten autoscaler max and add a grace policy to avoid mass scale-ups on noisy CI days. Long-term: split workloads and then we can model a 1-year partial reservation for steady portion.

ken (SRE): FYI: if we reserve too much and eviction/backoff behavior changes, app-level retries could drop, reducing hours. We should model both hours and retry-cost.

priya (CostOps): I'll produce a 3-scenario forecast by EOD: 1) status quo (spot heavy), 2) partial 1-yr reservation (steady 60%), 3) full reservation (unlikely). Will include net savings and sensitivity to eviction rate.

maya (FinOps): Perfect. Action items: Jordan -> infra ticket to split/pin persistent jobs (due 2026-03-27). Priya -> 3-scenario forecast (EOD today). Ashish -> restrict autoscaler spikes (ASAP). Maya -> update next-month committed capacity forecast once we have Priya's numbers.

jordan (Platform): Assigned INF-4398 for the split, will update here when done. :white_check_mark:

priya (CostOps): CSV and forecast link: gs://redwood-billing/analysis/asia-spot-reserved-2026-03.xlsx

maya (FinOps): Great — will wait for the forecast and then decide on a reserved buy. Thanks everyone. :bow:
